summary.headline: Mixed week: orders finished ahead of target at 102.9% while revenue reached only 90.2%, and Q1 closed behind at 92.4% of the quarter target.

points.what: Orders reached 855, or 102.9% of the weekly target, and the brief marks the level as notable against its recent range.
points.so_what: Order volume was not the constraint this week, so the revenue miss sits elsewhere in the mix.

points.what: Revenue was $61,356, or 90.2% of the weekly target, a gap of $6,650.
points.so_what: The final week of the quarter added to the quarter's shortfall rather than reducing it.

points.what: All three months of Q1 finished behind target, with January at 88.0% and March closest at 97.7%.
points.so_what: Attainment improved month by month, but no month covered its target, so the quarter's gap kept building.

points.what: Revenue was up 90.3% on last year, above the 75% growth the targets assume.
points.so_what: The year-on-year and the target comparisons point in opposite directions, so attainment is the measure to follow for this week.

points.what: AOV fell 5.2% to $83.03, a move rated bad.
points.so_what: Orders beat target while revenue did not, and order value is where the two diverge.

points.what: Reaching the full-year target requires $79,331 of revenue a week, against a current 8-week run-rate of $57,236.
points.so_what: The required pace sits far above the recent pace, so the full-year target is out of reach at this rate.

points.what: New signups of 236 were 3.7% below last year, a year-on-year move rated bad.
points.so_what: Signups are the one measure running below last year while orders are well ahead, a divergence to keep watching.

points.what: Orders came in at 102.9% of the weekly target while revenue reached 90.2%.
points.so_what: The week was mixed, and on the measure that feeds the quarter and the year it was behind.

points.what: QTD revenue finished at 92.4% of target, $58,998 short, with no weeks left in Q1.
points.so_what: The quarter can no longer be recovered, and the deficit carries straight into the year-to-date position.

points.what: With 40 weeks left, $3,173,245 remains against the full-year target of $3,888,802.
points.so_what: That leaves a weekly requirement well above the pace of the last eight weeks, so the year needs a step up rather than more of the same.

points.what: LATAM orders rose 40.2% to 122 and accounted for 134.6% of the week's order change.
points.so_what: The whole weekly order gain traces to one region, so the total is more concentrated than the headline increase suggests.

points.what: Search held 69.9% of orders but contributed only 2 orders to the change.
points.so_what: The largest source was essentially flat, so the week's increase came from elsewhere.

points.what: Email orders rose 31.4% to 46 and contributed 42.3% of the order change.
points.so_what: Order growth this week rests on sources that carry only a small share of total volume.

points.what: AOV was $83.03, down 5.2% on the week though 5.3% above last year.
points.so_what: Orders grew faster than revenue this week, and order value is where that difference shows.

points.what: The cancellation rate fell 2.8 pp to 13.6%, a change the brief marks as notable and good.
points.so_what: At $710 of revenue per percentage point, the lower rate worked in favour of a week that still missed its revenue target.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 09 Mar 2026 was 9.5%, up 0.3 pp and rated bad.
points.so_what: The uptick interrupts the downward path of the preceding weeks and is worth checking in the next mature week.

points.what: New signups rose 10.3% to 236, a notable weekly increase.
points.so_what: Signups grew faster than orders this week, which runs counter to their year-on-year direction.
